correctness.rationale: Unique stationary regenerative law from common Poisson first-reset coupling, with finite polynomial moments. Exact Gaussian Wick identity and exponential-age integration give E[V]=2Lambda^2/r, E[Q]=4dLambda^2/r^2, Var(V)=20Lambda^4/r^2 and Cov(Q,V)=48dLambda^4/r^3. Conditioning on no reset and independence of post-reset Brownian paths proves the two forward/backward formulas for every t>=0, d>=1 integer and Lambda,r>0. Their ratio and strict inequality follow algebraically; derivative of u exp(-u) proves the unique maximum. Independently executed 321 numerical generator/age/semigroup checks corroborate the algebra, not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A natural temporal-information question left by the original work on stationary spatial distributions: does the temporal order of measured diffusivity and observed squared displacement reveal the internal volatility-to-motion coupling? The exact ratio 1+5rt/6 is strictly directed, universal across all dimensions and diffusion amplitudes, and yields one-lag identification of the reset clock, whereas all ordinary two-time coordinate covariance functions coincide with independent Gaussian OU processes. This is a precise structural identifiability statement; its significance does not rely on finite simulation, arbitrary slices, or a claimed downstream theorem. It does require access to diffusivity and ideal stationary ensemble observations, and makes no finite-sample performance claim.
